## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

This PR speeds up decode and verify steps on the SM120/SM121 f16/bf16 forward engine (`sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120`). It builds on #1627, which gave the SM100 half flavors sink-free split partials and a combine that folds the sink once, and adds only what develop does not have yet. Three commits:

**1. SM120 sink split, whole-group PackGQA, SM120 combine price.**
- **Attention sink with split-KV.** The general, d256 and d512 f16/bf16 templates compile their sink fold out at `SPLIT_KV > 1` and write sink-free partials. #1627's sink combine entry then folds the sink once, as it does for the SM100 half flavors.
  - `Capabilities.split_sink` names the rows whose half kernels write such partials. It is set on the SM100 and SM120 f16/bf16 rows, and `mismatch()` and the split heuristics read it in place of develop's SM100 arch test. SM100 eligibility is unchanged.
  - The unsplit fold now keeps a row with no visible key and a `-inf` sink at O := 0, LSE := -inf instead of NaN.
- **Whole-group PackGQA.** A GQA group that does not divide the Q tile packs whole on the general and d256 templates: `q_tile // G` tokens per tile, with the remaining rows dead (no Q load, no O or Stats store).
  - `pack_gqa_group_size` / `pack_gqa_supported` gain a `tail=` contract, and `Capabilities.pack_gqa_tail_d_shapes` lists the flavors that implement it.
  - The kernels launch `ceil(S_q / (q_tile // G))` Q tiles, and `heuristics._split_launch` counts the same.
  - The causal mask covers the extra KV tile a tail-packed frontier can straddle.
  - Groups 5, 6, 7 and 12, which used to run unpacked and re-read the KV once per query head, now pack.
- **SM120 per-wave combine price.** The SM120 half row prices the split combine per wave at its own coefficient, `_SM120_SPLIT_KV_COMBINE_COST = 0.01` KV tiles, passed through a new trailing `combine_cost=` keyword of `choose_split_kv`. The B200 price, 0.1, charged a verify step's multi-wave combine up to a whole SM120 tile per partial and stopped it at split 2–4.
- **Base-2 Stats.** The d256 and d512 templates keep split partial LSEs natural-log when a direct caller enables base-2 Stats (Rule S4).

**2. SM120 packed decode tile.** A packed set used to ride the largest tile that admits the GQA ratio, 128 rows. For SM120 decode and verify, the 64-row tile is faster on most shapes: it carries fewer dead rows and, past 64 live rows, twice the units.
- `_sm120_tiles(..., pack_g)` picks 128 rows only when `S_q · G ≥ 128` and the 128-row units fill the machine with splits of two or more KV tiles; otherwise it picks 64 rows.
- Packing is still decided on the 128-row tile, so `64 ≤ S_q < 128` keeps its plan.
- Tile runners cover every tile except the lead's own, and the half row's runners are rescored to their own split.
- Measured on 80 b = 1 shapes per GPU, with every packed tile × split timed, the geomean regret against the ladder best falls from 1.28 to 1.04 on an RTX PRO 6000 and from 1.30 to 1.02 on an RTX 5080.

**3. Half-partial combine form.** #1627 tuned the combine's lean, serial and decode forms on fp32 partials. SM120 splits write half partials, which those forms read one element at a time.
- Half partials now take a half form at every S_q and split count:
  - one warp per row;
  - LSE passes that stride the split axis across the lanes, 32 splits a round;
  - an O pass that loads each split's four columns as one 8-byte vector, eight splits in flight.
- The sink and Q-length entries fold exactly as before, and fp32 partials keep develop's forms unchanged.
- Half partials are written by every SM120 split, the SM100 MXFP8 d512 split and the cc 10.7 flavors without an fp32 partial slot.
- The SM120 half row no longer charges #1627's B200-fitted serial-walk split price, which models a form its partials never take.

## Why

On an RTX PRO 6000, FROST's default plan ran at a geomean 0.75× of llama.cpp's FlashAttention kernels over 744 f16 decode and verify shapes from real models (kernel time, cold L2, one process per case). Two gaps were structural:
- **Sinks never split on SM120.** A gpt-oss-20b decode step (64/8 heads, d64, sink) at 64K KV ran on 8 CTAs: 1173 µs, against 133 µs for llama.cpp.
- **GQA 6 ran unpacked.** A Qwen3.6-27B decode step (24/4 heads, d256) at 64K KV re-read the KV once per query head: 524 µs, against 245 µs for llama.cpp.

After those, the split combine and the split depth were the next costs at decode.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API signature or dependency changes. The engine stays opt-in (`CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`). No native binding source changes: SM120 sink splits ride #1627's binder.
- New eligibility on SM 12.x f16/bf16:
  - dense unpadded sink graphs may split their KV;
  - GQA groups that do not divide the Q tile may pack, on the general and d256 flavors.
- `sm100/split_combine.py` is shared, so the SM100 MXFP8 d512 split and the cc 10.7 half-partial splits also take the half form.
  - B200 combine microbenchmark: 1.36× warm, 1.41× after an L2 scrub (below).
  - Those rows keep the B200 serial split price; they are unmeasured with the half form, see follow-ups.
- SM121 is admitted by the cc 12.x row but not validated.

## Performance

Paired A/B against `develop` at 90803d73a, on a GeForce RTX 5080 (cc 12.0, 84 SMs) and an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (cc 12.0, 188 SMs). The branch is on 6e5956abf, whose only commit since then (#1666) touches no SDPA forward file.
- Default plan (the first `OPENSOURCE` plan) on both sides.
- SM clock locked at 85% of max and memory clock at max; five alternating develop / this-PR process pairs; median of per-pair speedups (develop time / this-PR time).
- Kernel-time sums (attention + split combine): warm L2 is the mean of 50 calls, cold L2 is the median of 15 after a 256 MiB scrub.
- 120 decode/verify shapes: 5 families × S_kv 1K / 4K / 16K / 64K × S_q 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32, batch 1, f16. Plus 5 prefill shapes (S_q = S_kv = 8192) as a no-regression check.
- Every data point passes the between-run CV gate (≤ 5% on both legs).

**RTX 5080, b = 1, warm L2** (cold in parentheses):

| Family (H_q / H_kv, d) | S_q = 1 geomean | S_q 2–32 geomean | Range (warm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss: 64/8, d64, sink | 9.20× (7.42×) | 6.86× (5.92×) | 2.38–13.21× |
| GQA 6: 24/4, d128 | 4.36× (3.66×) | 3.31× (2.92×) | 1.51–7.02× |
| d256: 16/2 | 1.51× (1.39×) | 1.70× (1.57×) | 1.00–3.22× |
| qwen: 32/4, d128 | 1.57× (1.43×) | 1.65× (1.49×) | 1.00–2.72× |
| llama: 32/8, d128 | 1.60× (1.40×) | 1.66× (1.44×) | 1.00–2.65× |
| **All 120** | **2.73× (2.37×)** | **2.54× (2.25×)** | **1.001–13.21×** |

- 111 of 120 shapes are at least 3% faster, none is slower (minimum 1.001×), and the 5 prefill shapes measure 1.000×.
- Batched decode, b = 4 and b = 16 (llama, qwen, GQA 6, gpt-oss × S_kv 4K / 16K × S_q 1 / 8; 16 shapes each): 2.51× (2.17×) and 2.05× (2.06×) geomean; every shape is faster, the least by 1.31× (cold, b = 4).
- Examples (warm):
  - gpt-oss S_q 1 at 64K KV: 1655 → 153 µs;
  - GQA 6 S_q 1 at 64K KV: 647 → 155 µs;
  - llama S_q 32 at 1K KV: 31.9 → 12.0 µs;
  - qwen S_q 1 at 4K KV: 17.4 → 11.1 µs;
  - llama S_q 8 at 16K KV: 108.0 → 61.3 µs.

**RTX PRO 6000, b = 1, warm L2** (cold in parentheses):

| Family (H_q / H_kv, d) | S_q = 1 geomean | S_q 2–32 geomean | Range (warm) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| gpt-oss: 64/8, d64, sink | 10.72× (6.70×) | 8.34× (5.95×) | 2.57–22.28× |
| GQA 6: 24/4, d128 | 3.12× (2.05×) | 2.51× (1.90×) | 1.18–6.36× |
| d256: 16/2 | 1.46× (1.23×) | 1.54× (1.35×) | 1.02–1.93× |
| qwen: 32/4, d128 | 1.53× (1.22×) | 1.55× (1.32×) | 1.01–2.24× |
| llama: 32/8, d128 | 1.35× (1.12×) | 1.42× (1.18×) | 1.00–2.10× |
| **All 120** | **2.52× (1.87×)** | **2.35× (1.88×)** | **1.003–22.28×** |

- 108 of 120 shapes are at least 3% faster, none is slower (minimum 1.003×), and the 5 prefill shapes measure 0.999× (cold 0.998×), within noise.
- Batched decode, b = 4 and b = 16: 2.64× (1.67×) and 1.59× (1.34×) geomean; every shape is faster, the least by 1.007×.
- Examples (warm):
  - gpt-oss S_q 1 at 64K KV: 927 → 42 µs;
  - GQA 6 S_q 1 at 64K KV: 238 → 37 µs;
  - llama S_q 32 at 1K KV: 13.0 → 7.3 µs;
  - qwen S_q 1 at 4K KV: 11.7 → 8.1 µs;
  - llama S_q 8 at 16K KV: 32.9 → 20.1 µs.

**Combine kernel alone, half partials** (`compile_ptr` pointer entry; b = 1; 64 / 32 / 16 / 8 heads at d64 / d128 / d256 / d512; S_q 1–32; 4–64 splits; three alternating develop / this-PR process pairs, clocks locked, CV ≤ 3.5%):
- RTX 5080, 90 shapes (d64–d256): 1.19× warm, 1.13× scrubbed.
  - 1.1–1.3× at 8 splits;
  - 1.7–1.9× at S_q = 2 with 32–64 splits (d128: 4.9 → 2.9 µs at 32);
  - within 0.2 µs of develop at 4 splits.
- RTX PRO 6000, the same 90 shapes: 1.16× warm, 1.11× scrubbed (1.24× at 8 splits, 1.29–1.33× at 32–64; 0.96× at 4 splits warm and 0.92× at 16 splits scrubbed).
- B200, 120 shapes (d64–d512): 1.36× warm, 1.41× scrubbed.
  - Slower only at 4 splits (0.90–0.96×, at most 0.5 µs);
  - and scrubbed at S_q = 1 with 64 splits (0.91–0.94×).

**SM120 split model**, against an RTX 5080 split ladder (180 shapes: d64–d256, S_q 1–32, b 1/4/16, S_kv 1K–64K, every power-of-two split timed around the default plan):
- Per-wave price 0.01 instead of B200's 0.1: mean regret 5.8% → 0.9%. Any value in [0.0025, 0.03] makes the same choices, and each of the 23 it moves lands within 3% of the ladder best.
- No serial-walk term on the SM120 half row: mean regret 1.55% → 0.89%. The 5 choices it moves (d256 S_q 4–16 at 1K–4K KV) run 1.13–1.39× faster.
- The remaining regret is batched S_q = 32 (see follow-ups).
- The same ladder on the RTX PRO 6000 confirms the fit independently: the shipped prices give 0.97% mean regret (b = 1: 0.79%), against 1.64% with the serial term and 4.54% at the B200 prices. What remains is warm-L2 under-splitting on the 64-row tile at 4K–64K KV (see follow-ups).

## Testing

From `test/python`:

```
pytest -m 'L0 or L1' \
  sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm120.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_split_kv_sm120.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_fp8_sm120.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_mxfp8_sm120.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_native_sm120_binding.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_sm120.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_sm120_fp8.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_sm120_mxfp8.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_staged_forward_sm120.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_staged_sm120_mxfp8.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_native_dense_binding.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_native_split_binding.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_flashinfer_shaped_sdpa.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_prepared_mxfp8.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_heuristics.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_split_kv_heuristic.py sdpa/frost/test_heuristic_geometry.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_graph_analyzer.py \
  sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_sm100.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_half.py sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_many_splits.py
```

- **GeForce RTX 5080 (cc 12.0):** 3552 passed, 517 skipped, 0 failed. The skips are SM100-only suites and device guards.
  - Then, on the final head, the half-form combine tests plus the SM120 split suite: 427 passed, 0 failed.
- **RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (cc 12.0), final head:** 3762 passed, 487 skipped, 0 failed.
- **B200-class GPU (cc 10.0):** 0 failed in every run.
  - The combine and split suites (`test_sdpa_split_combine_half.py`, `test_sdpa_split_combine_sm100.py`, `test_sdpa_split_combine_many_splits.py`, `test_sdpa_fwd_split_kv_sm100.py`, `test_sdpa_native_split_binding.py`, `test_sdpa_prepared_fp8_split.py`, `test_sdpa_split_combine_artifact_cache.py`): 770 passed, 96 skipped.
  - The sink and split cases of the SM100 decode d128 / d256, split-KV and DSL suites: 1270 passed, 4 skipped.
  - The widened half-form tests: 374 passed.
- **Heuristics and contracts, CPU:** 1915 passed (adds `test_sdpa_fwd_placement.py`).

New coverage:
- **Sink with split:**
  - `test_sm120_split_folds_the_sink_once` covers every half template, decode and verify rows, packed and unpacked, split and unsplit.
  - `test_sm120_sink_rows_without_keys` covers rows whose keys all miss split 0, rows with no key at all, and `-inf` sinks, split and unsplit, with NaN-poisoned O and Stats.
  - `test_sm120_half_decode_splits_a_sink_and_packs_a_whole_group` checks that a half row without `split_sink` declines the sink split.
- **Tail packing:**
  - `test_sm120_tail_packed_tiles` pins top-left causal tiles whose frontier straddles an extra KV tile, windows with split, `S_q` values where the token-tile count differs from `ceil(S_q·G / q_tile)`, and both d256 Q tiles.
  - `test_sm120_tail_packed_launch_counts_token_tiles` pins the Q-tile count the split model sees.
- **Half form** (`test_sdpa_split_combine_half.py`, new; runs on the SM100 and SM120 lines through `requires_split_combine`):
  - f16 / bf16 partials;
  - S_q 1 / 2 / 5 and 2–100 splits, on and off both strides;
  - d 128 / 64 / 192, which exercises lanes past `d_v` and a second column round, and d 66 for element loads;
  - dead splits with NaN payloads;
  - plain, sink, and sink with Q lengths;
  - FP8 O with scale and amax.
- **Heuristics:**
  - `test_sm120_packed_set_rides_the_packed_launch_tile_rule`;
  - `test_sm120_prices_a_verify_combine_per_sm120_tile`;
  - `test_sm120_half_row_prices_no_serial_combine_walk`;
  - `test_split_chooser_receives_the_row_cost_profile`, which now also pins `serial_combine`.

## Follow-ups

- The other rows with half partials (SM120 FP8 / MXFP8 splits, the SM100 MXFP8 d512 split, the cc 10.7 flavors without an fp32 slot) also take the half form but keep the B200 serial-walk split price, which is unmeasured against that form. They may split shallower than their best.
- The split model's wave term still uses the B200 per-CTA cost (`_SPLIT_KV_CTA_COST = 21` KV tiles). On the RTX 5080 it under-splits batched S_q = 32 (b = 4/16: 6–21% regret) and gpt-oss S_q = 32 at 64K KV (10%). On the RTX PRO 6000 the 64-row tile at 4K–64K KV takes 16 splits where 32–64 run 9–17% faster warm (qwen S_q 1 at 4K: 8.1 against 7.1 µs). An SM120 per-CTA cost is a separate fit.
- The SM120 FP8 / MXFP8 / d512-FP8 sink folds have the same keyless-row `-inf`-sink NaN that this PR fixes in the half templates. It is pre-existing and not touched here.

## Affected area

## Summary

This PR speeds up decode and verify steps on the SM120/SM121 f16/bf16 forward engine (`sdpa_fwd_prefill_sm120`). It builds on #1627, which gave the SM100 half flavors sink-free split partials and a combine that folds the sink once, and adds only what develop does not have yet. Three commits:

**1. SM120 sink split, whole-group PackGQA, SM120 combine price.**
- **Attention sink with split-KV.** The general, d256 and d512 f16/bf16 templates compile their sink fold out at `SPLIT_KV > 1` and write sink-free partials. #1627's sink combine entry then folds the sink once, as it does for the SM100 half flavors.
  - `Capabilities.split_sink` names the rows whose half kernels write such partials. It is set on the SM100 and SM120 f16/bf16 rows, and `mismatch()` and the split heuristics read it in place of develop's SM100 arch test. SM100 eligibility is unchanged.
  - The unsplit fold now keeps a row with no visible key and a `-inf` sink at O := 0, LSE := -inf instead of NaN.
- **Whole-group PackGQA.** A GQA group that does not divide the Q tile packs whole on the general and d256 templates: `q_tile // G` tokens per tile, with the remaining rows dead (no Q load, no O or Stats store).
  - `pack_gqa_group_size` / `pack_gqa_supported` gain a `tail=` contract, and `Capabilities.pack_gqa_tail_d_shapes` lists the flavors that implement it.
  - The kernels launch `ceil(S_q / (q_tile // G))` Q tiles, and `heuristics._split_launch` counts the same.
  - The causal mask covers the extra KV tile a tail-packed frontier can straddle.
  - Groups 5, 6, 7 and 12, which used to run unpacked and re-read the KV once per query head, now pack.
- **SM120 per-wave combine price.** The SM120 half row prices the split combine per wave at its own coefficient, `_SM120_SPLIT_KV_COMBINE_COST = 0.01` KV tiles, passed through a new trailing `combine_cost=` keyword of `choose_split_kv`. The B200 price, 0.1, charged a verify step's multi-wave combine up to a whole SM120 tile per partial and stopped it at split 2–4.
- **Base-2 Stats.** The d256 and d512 templates keep split partial LSEs natural-log when a direct caller enables base-2 Stats (Rule S4).

**2. SM120 packed decode tile.** A packed set used to ride the largest tile that admits the GQA ratio, 128 rows. For SM120 decode and verify, the 64-row tile is faster on most shapes: it carries fewer dead rows and, past 64 live rows, twice the units.
- `_sm120_tiles(..., pack_g)` picks 128 rows only when `S_q · G ≥ 128` and the 128-row units fill the machine with splits of two or more KV tiles; otherwise it picks 64 rows.
- Packing is still decided on the 128-row tile, so `64 ≤ S_q < 128` keeps its plan.
- Tile runners cover every tile except the lead's own, and the half row's runners are rescored to their own split.
- Measured on 80 b = 1 shapes per GPU, with every packed tile × split timed, the geomean regret against the ladder best falls from 1.28 to 1.04 on an RTX PRO 6000 and from 1.30 to 1.02 on an RTX 5080.

**3. Half-partial combine form.** #1627 tuned the combine's lean, serial and decode forms on fp32 partials. SM120 splits write half partials, which those forms read one element at a time.
- Half partials now take a half form at every S_q and split count:
  - one warp per row;
  - LSE passes that stride the split axis across the lanes, 32 splits a round;
  - an O pass that loads each split's four columns as one 8-byte vector, eight splits in flight.
- The sink and Q-length entries fold exactly as before, and fp32 partials keep develop's forms unchanged.
- Half partials are written by every SM120 split, the SM100 MXFP8 d512 split and the cc 10.7 flavors without an fp32 partial slot.
- The SM120 half row no longer charges #1627's B200-fitted serial-walk split price, which models a form its partials never take.

## Why

On an RTX PRO 6000, FROST's default plan ran at a geomean 0.75× of llama.cpp's FlashAttention kernels over 744 f16 decode and verify shapes from real models (kernel time, cold L2, one process per case). Two gaps were structural:
- **Sinks never split on SM120.** A gpt-oss-20b decode step (64/8 heads, d64, sink) at 64K KV ran on 8 CTAs: 1173 µs, against 133 µs for llama.cpp.
- **GQA 6 ran unpacked.** A Qwen3.6-27B decode step (24/4 heads, d256) at 64K KV re-read the KV once per query head: 524 µs, against 245 µs for llama.cpp.

After those, the split combine and the split depth were the next costs at decode.

## API and compatibility impact

- No public API signature or dependency changes. The engine stays opt-in (`CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`). No native binding source changes: SM120 sink splits ride #1627's binder.
- New eligibility on SM 12.x f16/bf16:
  - dense unpadded sink graphs may split their KV;
  - GQA groups that do not divide the Q tile may pack, on the general and d256 flavors.
- `sm100/split_combine.py` is shared, so the SM100 MXFP8 d512 split and the cc 10.7 half-partial splits also take the half form.
  - B200 combine microbenchmark: 1.36× warm, 1.41× after an L2 scrub (below).

- SM121 is admitted by the cc 12.x row but not validated.

+        lse[:, :, :, 0] = -torch.inf

+        lse[32, :, :, sq - 1] = -torch.inf
